brief.offer: Onboarding email sequences for startup founders

facts.claim: Mercury says more than 300,000 customers use its product.
facts.excerpt: Today, more than 300,000 customers use Mercury.

facts.claim: Mercury says 1 in 3 U.S. startups use it, including a growing share of AI companies.
facts.excerpt: Today, 1 in 3 U.S. startups use Mercury, including a rapidly growing share of AI companies — in 2025, we onboarded 2.4x more AI companies than the year before.

facts.claim: Mercury says it built its business on a partner bank model and uses direct integrations with partner banks for banking services.
facts.excerpt: From the beginning, we’ve built Mercury with a partner bank business model. Today, we support over 300K customers, with banking services provided through Mercury’s direct integrations with our partner banks
facts.source_title: How Mercury works with its partners to bring you powerful banking | Mercury

facts.claim: Mercury offers free invoicing, with recurring invoices and ACH debit available on paid plans.
facts.excerpt: Customers can create, send, track, and receive payment on as many invoices as they’d like in the free version of Mercury. Advanced invoicing capabilities, such as sending recurring invoices, and invoicing with ACH debit, are available as part of our paid plans.

facts.claim: Mercury Bill Pay is an automated accounts payable product that lets companies manage bills from their Mercury account and pay by ACH, check, or wire.
facts.excerpt: Mercury Bill Pay is an automated accounts payable solution that helps you manage and pay company bills from your Mercury account. Bills sent to your dedicated inbox are automatically organized by approval status and due date, and can be scheduled for payment via ACH, check, or wire.

facts.claim: Mercury offers personal banking with 3.50% APY on savings, joint accounts, and unlimited free USD wires.
facts.excerpt:
Mercury for personal

Level up your personal finances with 3.50% APY on your savings account, joint accounts, unlimited free USD wires, and more.
facts.source_title: Online Business Banking For Startups, Small Businesses & Scaling Companies

facts.claim: Mercury has launched Mercury Books, described as AI-powered accounting software built into its product.
facts.excerpt: Introducing Mercury Books, AI-powered accounting software, built into Mercury
facts.source_title: Online Business Banking For Startups, Small Businesses & Scaling Companies

facts.claim: Mercury Insights provides business-account analytics with interactive charts, tables, AI-powered cashflow alerts, and a chatbot.
facts.excerpt: For business accounts, interactive charts and tables update automatically so you always know where things stand: filter and compare by time periods, get AI-powered cashflow alerts and ask a chatbot questions like “Why did expenses increase this month?”

research.website_note: The results show mercury.com is Mercury’s official site and repeatedly describe Mercury as the company behind it.

strategy.observation: Mercury says 1 in 3 U.S. startups use it, including a growing share of AI companies, which means a large share of its audience is startup founders rather than generic SMB users.
strategy.offer_link: Onboarding email sequences for startup founders could help Mercury guide that startup-heavy audience from account opening to first-value moments, especially if the goal is to improve activation and adoption across a founder-led customer base.
hypotheses: Mercury may want to increase early activation and reduce drop-off among new startup founders.
Mercury may need lifecycle messaging that explains product setup and the first few use cases in a founder-friendly way.
Mercury may be looking for ways to drive feature adoption across products like banking, invoicing, bill pay, or books through onboarding.
Mercury may have enough volume in this segment that even small gains in onboarding conversion would matter.
strategy.angle: Mercury already serves 1 in 3 U.S. startups, so a founder-specific onboarding sequence could be the fastest way to move new accounts from sign-up to first value.
strategy.fit_reason: The offer matches Mercury’s startup-founder-heavy customer base, making onboarding sequences for founders a plausible lever for activation and adoption. The fit is strong, though the specific internal need is still an assumption.

draft.subject: Founder onboarding idea
draft.body:
Hi — Mercury already says 1 in 3 U.S. startups use it, so my guess is a founder-specific onboarding sequence could do a lot of the early heavy lifting.

I write onboarding email sequences for startup founders, usually to help new accounts get from sign-up to first value without extra friction.

If you’re focused on activation this quarter, should I send over a simple 3-email outline built around founder sign-up and first use?
